sources.title: In vivo stimulation of connective tissue accumulation by the tripeptide-copper complex glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine-Cu2+ in rat experimental wounds
sources.keyFindings: GHK-Cu increased extracellular-matrix accumulation in rat wound chambers; this is not a human healing result.

sources.title: Effects of topical copper tripeptide complex on CO2 laser-resurfaced skin
sources.keyFindings: Among 13 completers, blinded objective outcomes did not differ between regimens; patient-rated skin quality favored the GHK-Cu regimen.

sources.title: A prospective randomized evaluator-blinded trial of two potential wound healing agents for the treatment of venous stasis ulcers
sources.keyFindings: In 86 evaluable patients, a tripeptide-copper 0.4% cream did not differ from vehicle for ulcer size; silver sulfadiazine reduced size more than either.

sources.title: A gene expression signature of emphysema-related lung destruction and its reversal by the tripeptide GHK
sources.keyFindings: GHK, rather than a tested GHK-Cu product, altered gene-expression and fibroblast responses in experimental systems; no patient treatment outcome was tested.

evidenceSummary.scope: The previous 35-record inventory was removed after identifier review. Four primary records used in the dossier were verified separately; they do not establish injected GHK-Cu efficacy.

notes: The previous 35-source inventory contained mismatched publication identifiers and unsupported clinical claims. Four independently checked dossier citations are retained; other records remain excluded until rebuilt from primary publications. The separately registered trial is not an efficacy result.

trials.title: Topical GHK-Cu Gel for Acute Skin Wound Healing
